recovered_records.title: DAO: Delay adversarial optimization gains domain-invariant feature of neural networks for automatic sleep staging
recovered_records.abstract: Sleep staging is a crucial link between brain function monitoring and regulation. Current deep learning-based methods have unlocked a new paradigm for feature learning in automatic sleep staging modeling. However, most deep learning models still lack robustness to the domain-invariant features of sleep signals. Making them unable to effectively address individual differences and data imbalance in the automatic sleep staging task. In this paper, we propose a delayed adversarial optimization neural network approach that can improve the learning of domain-invariant features in the automatic sleep staging task. Specifically, we introduce the simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF) of neural collapse to depict the domain-invariant features of sleep signals. Constraining the imbalanced staging features to align with the ETF of balanced data learning. Then, to simulate the data property of individual differences among different subjects, we generate adversarial minority samples by perturbing the loss of the staging model. In addition, an ETF joint optimization strategy is established to fine-tune the staging model, achieving the domain-invariant feature gain. We validated the proposed method on MASS and Sleep_EDF datasets under a cross-subject test experiment. The test results showed that our method has significant advantages in addressing the problem of individual differences.

recovered_records.title: DuKAN: A dual kolmogorov-arnold network with transformer for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting
recovered_records.abstract: Accurate ultra-short-term wind power forecasting is crucial for maintaining grid stability and facilitating the integration of renewable energy. This study introduces DuKAN (Dual Kolmogorov-Arnold Network), a novel neural architecture that integrates Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with transformer mechanisms for wind power prediction. DuKAN presents three key methodological contributions. First, a dual KAN layer is proposed by integrating TaylorKAN for local feature extraction and WaveKAN for multi-scale frequency analysis, enabling effective modeling of nonlinear temporal dependencies. Second, a dual-branch architecture is designed that leverages VMD-decomposed signals at different reconstruction levels: one branch processes smoother representations to capture primary trends, while the other processes detail-rich representations to preserve rapid fluctuations, thereby enhancing robustness against noise from complementary perspectives. Third, the designed dual KAN layer is incorporated into the transformer’s encoder-decoder framework, facilitating long-term dependency modeling through transformer mechanisms. Comprehensive experiments conducted across six real-world wind farms, representing diverse geographical conditions, demonstrate DuKAN’s superior performance. The method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all evaluation metrics, achieving improvements of up to 15.2% in offshore scenarios based on weighted average MAE compared to TFT. DuKAN maintains high stability across varying input lengths and prediction horizons, making it a robust solution for practical renewable energy forecasting applications.

recovered_records.title: Improved adaptive optimization algorithm for training physics-informed neural networks
recovered_records.abstract: Adaptive optimization methods are widely used for training deep neural networks, but their performance can deteriorate when the second-moment estimate is poorly scaled, often leading to unstable updates in stiff and ill-conditioned Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). To alleviate this issue, we develop AdaLB, an Adam-type optimizer that combines belief-based scaling with long-term gradient memory to stabilize adaptive updates. In AdaLB, the conventional second-moment estimate of squared gradients is replaced by an exponential moving average of gradient prediction errors, while a power-series-based accumulator is introduced to produce a time-varying decay factor for the second moment. Under the online convex optimization framework, we further establish an O(T) regret bound under standard assumptions. Experiments on synthetic objectives and PINN benchmarks, including the Burgers equation, Poisson equation, and a high-order differential equation, show that AdaLB is effective on the Burgers and Poisson problems and can also provide a stronger first-stage optimizer when combined with L-BFGS. The results also suggest that the role of long-term memory depends on the problem setting and on the choice of γ.

recovered_records.title: Prompt-driven transformer for brain tumor segmentation with missing modalities
recovered_records.abstract: Brain tumor segmentation from multi-modality magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays an important role in diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis evaluation. However, most existing deep learning methods assume that all MRI modalities are available, whereas in clinical practice some modalities may be missing due to motion artifacts, acquisition failure, or patient-specific factors. This missing-modality setting severely degrades segmentation performance, especially for the enhancing tumor region when the T1c modality is absent. To address this challenge, we propose a novel Prompt-driven Transformer, termed PDFormer, for unified brain tumor segmentation under arbitrary missing modality scenarios. Specifically, we design a Missing Modality Prompt Generator (MMPG) to learn a universal prompt and dynamically derive modality-state-aware prompts for different missing patterns. A Prompt-driven Integrator (PDI) is further introduced to progressively inject the prompt information into both intra-modality and inter-modality feature interactions, enabling the model to effectively exploit local and global contextual cues under incomplete inputs. Moreover, to alleviate the severe performance drop caused by the absence of the key T1c modality, we propose an Activator Generator (ActGen) that synthesizes compensatory modality-specific information through a self-distillation strategy. Extensive experiments on the public BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2021 datasets demonstrate that PDFormer consistently outperforms representative state-of-the-art methods across diverse missing modality settings. In addition, statistical analysis on the large-scale BraTS2021 benchmark confirms that the observed improvements are significant and robust. These results show that PDFormer provides an effective and practical solution for brain tumor segmentation with incomplete multi-modal MRI.

recovered_records.title: Convolution mixer-based transformer-style network for lightweight remote sensing image super-resolution
recovered_records.abstract: Recent developments in deep-learning-based remote sensing image super-resolution (RSISR) have attracted significant attention. In conventional models, upsampling is typically performed at the end of the architecture, which reduces computational cost but leads to loss of detail and degraded image quality. Furthermore, maintaining detail in remote sensing images is difficult due to their structural complexity and the variety of textures they contain. Although transformer-based methods improve the capture of global features, they often introduce redundancy and fail to capture local nuances. To address this issue, we propose a convolution-mixer-based transformer-style network for lightweight remote sensing image super-resolution (CMTSNSR). Convolutional modulation (Conv2Former), a simple block with linear (rather than quadratic) complexity compared to Transformers, forms the foundation of the proposed method. By using simple convolutions and the Hadamard product, Conv2Former simplifies the self-attention process. Additionally, the Conv2Former block is further enhanced to mix both spatial and channel locations using a convolution mixer. The convolution mixer uses three types of convolutions: a dilated depthwise convolution to increase the receptive field, a depthwise convolution to mix spatial locations, and a pointwise convolution to mix channel locations. We propose a convolutional modulation block (Conv2FormerB), comparable to the Transformer block, that combines Conv2Former with a multi-layer perceptron (MLP). For the RSISR challenge, a CMTSNSR is created using this Conv2FormerB, 3 × 3 convolution, and enhanced spatial attention (ESA) block. This CMTSNSR performed well across several RSISR benchmarks. Our CMTSNSR model achieves a runtime approximately 2.1× faster than Rep-Mamba.

recovered_records.title: Physics-informed hybrid digital twin for real-time multi-sensor intelligence and adaptive control in wire electrical discharge machining
recovered_records.abstract: In manufacturing settings, digital twins are advancing beyond static simulations to dynamic informatics systems that exhibit reasoning, flexibility and real-time control. This research proposes a physics-informed Hybrid Digital Twin (HDT) that integrated multi-sensor data (acoustic emission (AE), current, voltage and temperature) with machine-learning inference and real-time physics-informed constraints for process intelligence in Wire Electrical Discharge Machining (WEDM). The HDT architecture consists of five informatics layers: data acquisition, signal preprocessing, frequency domain reasoning (FFT–STFT–WPSD), features correlation analytics, and adaptive learning based control systems. Real-time experiments are presented based on 36 WEDM runs from AISI D2 steel, demonstrating AE_RMS as the most significant diagnostic feature (r = 0.99 with surface roughness), exceeding sensitivity and predictive reliability as compared to other data modalities based on time, frequency and time-frequency domains. Both Random Forest and ANN achieved R² > 0.95 and detection latency speed of under 20 ms, demonstrating the feasibility of a closed-loop control system. The adaptive decision logic was also constrained to maintain discharging current within ± 3% of nominal, directly causing a 4.9% improved material removal rate, keeping surface variation ≤ 5%, with wire rupturing incidents going reduced by 75%. The proposed approach HDT gives a self-learning, data–physics fusion architecture for system observability, real-time adaptation and zero defect manufacturing – an architect created for Industry 4.0 to adapt multi-sensor data informatics and autonomous machining intelligence.

recovered_records.title: Two-level breast tumor classification with multi-view imaging and pathology-aware large language models: A fuzzy KNN and ensemble learning framework
recovered_records.abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most prevalent cancers among women, and its accurate and timely diagnosis requires the use of intelligent decision-making algorithms. In the present study, a two-level framework based on mammography images and pathological textual data is proposed, with the purpose of enhancing the accuracy of classifying benign and malignant tumors. At the first level, the framework generates three independent representations, namely the HSV color space, heatmap, and thermal color map, from the original mammography images to provide a multi-view representation of the target tissue. For each modality independently, the framework extracts classical texture features such as LBP, GLCM, and HOG, along with deep features derived from pre-trained neural networks. The framework subsequently applies principal component analysis (PCA) separately to each image view to reduce dimensionality and eliminate statistical noise. The proposed framework subsequently feeds the reduced outputs into a Fuzzy k-nearest neighbor’s algorithm, which classifies the samples into healthy or suspicious categories based on their imaging features. At the second level, the framework analyzes only the samples identified as suspicious in the first level using textual data. In this stage, the pathology reports corresponding to each sample, after undergoing linguistic preprocessing including cleaning and normalization, are provided to an aggregation-based approach employing large language models, and the process of feature extraction is carried out. The semantic vectors extracted from the large language models undergo PCA-based dimensionality reduction before being fed into a Fuzzy k-NN classifier for final tumor classification (benign/malignant). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy, shows robustness against noisy data, and effectively manages borderline cases. These findings highlight its potential as a reliable clinical decision-support system for breast cancer diagnosis.

recovered_records.title: Bridging physics and machine learning: AI-enhanced WRF ensemble approach to extreme rainfall prediction
recovered_records.abstract: Extreme weather remains poorly predicted globally due to the rarity, rapid intensification, and inadequate representation in numerical models, thereby limiting forecast skill. With the frequency of extremes rising, reliable forecasts with sufficient lead-time are essential for disaster mitigation. Here, we evaluate rainfall forecasts by integrating AI with Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model ensembles during the catastrophic Kerala flood of 14–16 August 2018. Optimized WRF parameterization enhances baseline skill, while En3DVar data assimilation further improves spatial correlation against IMD daily observations from 0.09 to 0.30 (Domain 2, Δ = +0.21) and from 0.10 to 0.69 (Domain 1, Δ = +0.59) for the peak flood day (16 August). We introduce a hybrid WRFDA–Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework that integrates En3DVar-corrected WRF outputs with deep learning post-processing for regional extreme rainfall forecasting, an approach that, to our knowledge, has not been previously demonstrated for convection-permitting ensemble rainfall prediction over complex orographic terrain, which achieves final spatial correlations of 0.69 (Domain 1) and 0.66 (Domain 2) against IMD daily observations, representing total improvements of Δ = +0.59 and Δ = +0.57 respectively over the WRF standalone baseline, with additional LSTM contributions of Δ = +0.00 (Domain 1) and Δ = +0.36 (Domain 2) over WRFDA alone. The LSTM further reduces mean absolute error to 37.90 mm day⁻¹ (Domain 1) and 42.73 mm day⁻¹ (Domain 2) against IMD, compared to 63.85 and 66.81 mm day⁻¹ for the WRF standalone, reductions of 41% and 36% respectively. Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency improves from −0.88 to 0.44 (Domain 1) and from −1.01 to 0.40 (Domain 2), confirming forecast skill beyond a simple mean reference. Both spatial correlations are statistically significant at the 5% level (p < 0.05; p = 2.52 ×10⁻⁵ and 3.85 ×10⁻⁵ respectively) after accounting for spatial autocorrelation. This fusion of physics-based modelling and deep learning significantly advances extreme rainfall forecasting, offering operationally feasible applicability in tropical regions experiencing rapid climate shifts.

recovered_records.title: Adaptive graph convolution neural networks with spatial and frequency domain attention mechanism for traffic flow forecasting
recovered_records.abstract: Traffic flow prediction plays a crucial role in alleviating traffic congestion and low carbon emission. The inherent complexity and dynamic nature of traffic flow prediction pose challenges to accurate traffic flow prediction. Recent Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), their variant Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated effectiveness in modeling complicated spatial-temporal dependencies and achieved promising result. However, existing approaches relying on static node adjacency relationships and often struggle to leverage sophisticated spatial-temporal architecture design, which constrained the prediction precision. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a simple traffic flow prediction framework that integrates three innovative components: 1) a spatial attention mechanism to characterize global spatial dependencies, 2) dynamically adaptive graph convolutional node embedding where attention-derived node similarities serve as dynamic adjacency matrices, and 3) a frequency-domain attention mechanism for efficient temporal feature processing. Comprehensive experiments conducted on three real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of our model: (1) For 15-min short-term prediction, MAE/RMSE metrics show better results compared with baseline optimal performance; (2) 30-min mid-term prediction achieves significant MAE/RMSE improvement; (3) While 60-min long-term prediction exhibits a slight RMSE increase; (4) Considering integrated short/mid/long-term performance, the proposed model achieves obvious overall MAE/RMSE reduction on test sets. These results validate the effectiveness of our approach in balancing prediction accuracy across multiple temporal horizons.

recovered_records.title: H-Net: A transformer based multistage fusion convolutional neural network for underwater object detection in complex environments
recovered_records.abstract: Underwater Object Detection (UOD) has gained significant attention in recent years due to its critical role in applications such as oceanographic research, marine resource management, and underwater surveillance. However, UOD remains challenging because of complex underwater conditions, including light scattering, low visibility, and object occlusion. These factors degrade image quality and make it difficult to accurately detect and classify objects across varying depths and environmental conditions. To tackle this issue, this paper presents the Transformer based Multi-Stage Fusion Convolutional Neural Network (TransMSFCNNet) named H-Net model where the symbol ‘H’ is used to refer to its hierarchical architecture which incorporates convolutional and transformer-based multistage fusion to achieve powerful UOD in challenging settings. The main modules that have been used in H-Net model are the Dynamic Convolutional Feature Extraction Module (DCFEM) which extracts key features and the Attention-Guided Fusion Module (AGFM) which focuses on the most pertinent features by utilizing attention mechanisms that integrate both spatial and depth related information. Multistage Pooling Module (MSPM) minimizes the spatial dimensions, yet retained important information to represent long-range interactions and avoid overfitting. Transformer-Based Multistage Fusion Module (TMFM) aims at taking extra attention to fine-grained local correlations and feature interactions on various levels, enhancing the capability of more accurately detecting underwater objects. Meanwhile, Depth-Adaptive Object Detection Module (DAODM) dynamically scales the process of object detection according to the depth of objects, further boosting the object detection in low-contrast and high-occlusion parts of underwater scenes. Multistage Loss Function (MSL) optimizes classification and localization and deals with the imbalance between classes to achieve robust classification. The benefits of the H-Net model are associated with weaker impact of environmental interference, better analysis of intricate underwater scenes, and enhanced recognition of small or partially obscured objects. The proposed H-Net model is evaluated on four standard underwater benchmark datasets i.e., RUOD, URPC2023, UTDAC2020, and S-UODAC2020 which achieves mAP@[.5:.95] of 0.942, 0.940, 0.938, and 0.946, and F1-scores of 96.1%, 95.8%, 95.7%, and 95.9%, respectively.

recovered_records.title: A hybrid method based on linear regression and genetic programming-based symbolic regression for short-term load forecasting
recovered_records.abstract: Accurate short-term load forecasting (STLF) is critical for optimizing energy scheduling and ensuring grid stability, particularly in increasingly complex and volatile operational conditions. Existing methods often face challenges in interpretability, feature engineering and generalization. Traditional models lack transparency and fail to uncover the underlying drivers of load variation, while complex nonlinear models rely on numerous parameters, increasing overfitting risk and limiting practical applicability. To address these challenges, this paper presents a hybrid framework, LR-GPSR, which integrates linear regression (LR) with genetic programming-based symbolic regression (GPSR). This method first employs LR to generate initial load predictions and compute residuals, then applies GP to model these residuals, effectively capturing nonlinear patterns. In this study, LR-GPSR extends the basic arithmetic operators (addition, subtraction, and multiplication) used in SGP-1 by incorporating a logarithmic function, addressing the limited expressive capacity of the original set and providing sufficient representation for modeling residuals. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets show that the logarithmic function improves the quality of individuals generated during population initialization, enhancing the overall initial population. Comparative experiments further demonstrate that LR-GPSR outperforms traditional methods under high-load conditions with pronounced nonlinear characteristics, validating its effectiveness and robustness, and highlighting its potential to improve STLF reliability and support intelligent grid management.

recovered_records.title: Federated learning enhanced spatial and temporal attention mechanism for multivariate time series anomaly detection
recovered_records.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) deployments generate high-dimensional multivariate time series (MTS) in which anomalies are rare yet safety-critical; however, privacy and governance constraints often restrict centralizing raw sensor streams, motivating decentralized anomaly detection for multivariate time series (ADMTS). We propose FL-STAM, a federated learning (FL) framework that detects anomalies by learning and contrasting spatial (cross-sensor) and temporal (within-window) association patterns while keeping data local. FL-STAM adopts a factorized design with two parallel complete graphs—a sensor-wise (serial-oriented) graph and a time-wise graph—and applies graph attention to capture global inter-sensor coupling and window-level temporal dynamics. The resulting representations are processed by a dual-branch Transformer that produces content-based spatial attention and a Gaussian-kernel temporal association (with a learnable bandwidth), enabling explicit association modeling under a temporal locality prior. Their discrepancy is quantified via a layer-aggregated symmetric Wasserstein distance and stabilized by an alternating minimize/maximize training schedule with stop-gradient to prevent degenerate solutions. Under Federated Averaging (FedAvg), clients exchange only model updates, so raw measurements remain on-device for privacy-aware deployment. Experiments on five public IIoT benchmarks against eight representative baselines, evaluated using Precision, Recall, and F1, show consistent improvements; FL-STAM attains a mean F1 of 96.82 across datasets.

recovered_records.title: HaloSeg: Halo transformer embedding U-Net for local-global feature induced semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images
recovered_records.abstract: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing (HRRS) images has become a hot topic but with large difficulties owing to variable target scales, similar object interference, and partial occlusion. The remarkable successes of hybrid models of convolutional neural network and transformer indicate the necessity of integrating local contexts and global dependencies. However, insufficient mining and fusion of local and global features remain the main defects for current models. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel halo transformer embedding U-Net semantic segmentation model (HaloSeg). It constitutes a parallel dual-encoder architecture by coupling halo transform with residual network for global and local expression learning separately to avoid mutual interference in hierarchical feature extraction, with a shared decoder constructed for semantic prediction based on the fused features. First, an innovative halo transformer is constructed based on an improved multiscale halo self-attention to fully exploit distant dependencies within different enlarged receptive fields and adaptively fuse them to produce expressive global features. Second, a dual attention fusion (DAF) module is developed to further enhance global and local expressions and precisely fuse their complementarity to generate informative features for each layer, thus improving model discriminability. Third, an adaptive spatial structure mining (SSM) module is designed to learn multiscale and deformable expressions from primary convolutional feature to mitigate detail loss of high-level semantic features to promote more accurate semantic prediction. The experimental results on three public HRRS datasets demonstrate that HaloSeg significantly outperforms the other state-of-the-art models and is a promising tool for semantic segmentation.

recovered_records.title: Solving the time-dependent agile earth observation satellite scheduling problem using adaptive large neighborhood search with reinforcement learning controller
recovered_records.abstract: The Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling Problem (AEOSSP) entails the selection and scheduling of observation tasks from a candidate list to maximize profits. While Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) is a prominent method for addressing this problem, its reliance on hand-crafted selectors for neighborhood transformation operators often results in inefficient weight updates, thereby limiting its overall performance. To address this issue, we propose a Reinforcement Learning Enhanced ALNS (RL-ALNS) for efficient AEOSSP resolution. RL-ALNS is a lightweight yet effective framework that dynamically prioritizes operators by considering scenario-specific demands and real-time performance during the search process. It integrates a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-enhanced controller to optimize operator selection and incorporates multiple problem-specific position operators (POs) into the ALNS framework to enable efficient task insertion. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of RL-ALNS over the state-of-the-art Tabu-based ALNS Algorithm (ALNS/TPF). Specifically, RL-ALNS achieves a 2.3% higher profit rate on average and consistently outperforms ALNS/TPF in the early stages of the search process. Further experiments reveal that the RL-enhanced controller significantly improves operator selection efficiency, while the POs ensure stable and high-quality task insertion. These findings highlight the superior performance of RL-ALNS in tackling the AEOSSP, establishing it as a significant advancement over conventional methodologies in satellite scheduling optimization, while also demonstrating its potential for addressing complex, real-world scheduling challenges across diverse domains.

recovered_records.title: PHOG-Net: An interpretable and efficient hybrid CNN framework for medical image classification using gradient histogram integration
recovered_records.abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have proven effective in medical image classification, but they often struggle to capture fine textures and directional patterns that are important for accurate diagnosis. To address this challenge, PHOG-Net was developed by integrating Pyramid Histogram of Oriented Gradients (PHOG) into the network. Instead of adding handcrafted features after feature extraction, the model embeds gradient-based descriptors within the CNN, which improves interpretability and sensitivity to diagnostic texture cues. The architecture uses a dual-path stem layer and a sequence of PHOG Processing Blocks to extract spatial representations together with gradient-based texture features. These blocks combine 2D and 1D convolutional layers with fixed PHOG descriptors, which allows the model to capture multi-scale information. Although the feature capacity is expanded, the overall design remains lightweight, requiring far fewer parameters than DenseNet121, VGG16, and ResNet-18. Performance was assessed across 12 MedMNIST datasets and compared against standard CNNs, Vision Transformers, and AutoML-generated architectures. PHOG-Net showed strong performance across these tasks. Accuracy scores of 82.80% and 92.4% were achieved on OCTMNIST and PathMNIST, respectively, while AUC values of 0.998 and 0.995 were recorded for OrganAMNIST and OrganCMNIST. Across 12 MedMNIST benchmarks, PHOG-Net achieves up to 0.87% higher classification accuracy than leading state-of-the-art models, while using less than half the learnable parameters of ResNet-18. SmoothGrad saliency maps further confirmed that the model focuses on clinically relevant regions. PHOG-Net offers an efficient and texture-sensitive alternative to conventional CNNs and transformer-based models. By incorporating PHOG-based gradient information within the CNN architecture, several limitations of standard convolutional representations are reduced. The source code supporting this study is publicly available at: https://github.com/EbrahimAlwajih/phognet.

recovered_records.title: An asynchronous parallel symbolic regression approach based on multiobjective genetic programming with GPU acceleration
recovered_records.abstract: Symbolic regression is an explainable machine learning approach to data analysis, which aims to distill analytical data-driven models that are represented as mathematical expressions by optimizing both the parameters and structure. Commonly used genetic programming based symbolic regression algorithms often suffer from low efficiency and the effects of blind search, model bloat and diversity loss when dealing with massive data. This paper improves the performance of genetic programming based symbolic regression algorithms via handling these effects, task parallelism and hardware acceleration. We propose an asynchronous parallel framework based on multiobjective genetic programming algorithms, in which problem decomposition and elite sharing strategies are used to quickly produce various high-quality models and crosswise evolve elite models among different subtasks. In this way, such cross-evolution of elite models among subtasks can improve the model generalization, evolving efficiency and population diversity. Moreover, a tailor-made hybrid CPU-GPU acceleration strategy based on the compute unified device architecture is designed for the proposed algorithm by offloading model evaluations and, reducing the memory usage pressure and the communications between the CPU and GPUs. Ablation and comparison experiments are conducted to evaluate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate the positivity and effectiveness in data depiction, bloat-control and time-efficiency of the proposed framework. The proposed algorithm framework achieves 6.5-12.4× speedup for ground-truth problems and 5.1-13.4× for black-box problems with CPU implementations respectively and, accordingly 6.1-365.5× and 4.4-188.4× speedup with CPU-GPU implementations against the standard multiobjective genetic programming based symbolic regression algorithm in terms of average model exploration rate. Accelerated by two GPUs, it achieves 2.6-28.2× and 2.6-15.2× speedup for the proposed asynchronous parallel approach on the ground-truth and black-box benchmarks with large datasets respectively.

recovered_records.title: A prediction method for complex medium fields based on a multi-scale Physics-Informed Neural Network integrated with adversarial training
recovered_records.abstract: In fields closely related to national strategic needs, such as energy development, environmental protection, and geological engineering, the accurate prediction of the physical response field from complex medium fields is a core scientific issue for achieving key engineering tasks. Although Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) provide a new paradigm by embedding physical constraints, they struggle to effectively decouple the differences in medium parameter heterogeneity across multiple orders of magnitude. Moreover, they lack robustness when facing input perturbations such as sensor noise. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Multi-scale Physics-Informed Neural Network with Adversarial Training (AM-PINN). This approach is based on a Dense Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network, integrating the U-Net architecture, the Parallel Hybrid Multi-scale Convolutional Aggregator (PHMCA), and the Dynamic Field-Aware Pyramid Pooling Module (DFAPP), and adopts an adversarial training strategy based on the joint gradient of physical constraint residuals and boundary conditions. During the learning process. The results show that AM-PINN significantly improves the prediction accuracy of the pressure field and flux field in the case of small samples (512, 1024, 2048, 4096). Meanwhile, the model's excellent performance on the high-resolution test set demonstrates its superior generalization ability. In addition, by introducing adversarial training, the model's robustness against measurement noise has also been enhanced.

recovered_records.title: Physics-informed gated network for solving nonlinear partial differential equations
recovered_records.abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are extensively utilized to describe physical phenomena across diverse fields and play an essential role in scientific research. Recently, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have exhibited considerable potential in providing highly accurate numerical solutions to PDEs. Motivated by PINNs, this paper proposes Physics-Informed Gated Networks (PIGNs) for solving PDEs. PIGNs replace the conventional network architecture of PINNs with Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). This modification enables PIGNs to capture and retain temporal dependencies more effectively. Additionally, a Regional Weight Optimization (RWO) strategy is introduced to PIGNs to optimize the weights assigned to different regions. The RWO strategy consists of a stepwise-weighting mechanism and a modified learning rate annealing algorithm. The stepwise-weighting mechanism generates local multipliers that assign greater weights to information-intensive intermediate regions and challenging termination moment regions during the optimization process. The modified learning rate annealing algorithm generates global multipliers for balancing different loss terms. Finally, the performance of PIGNs and the RWO strategy is evaluated by learning solutions of the convection–diffusion equation, the Korteweg-de Vries equation, the Nonlinear Schrödinger equation and the Chen-Lee-Liu equation. The experimental results show that PIGNs provide more accurate predictions than PINNs. Furthermore, the RWO strategy enhances the accuracy of PIGNs.

recovered_records.title: TIH: Transformer in hyperbolic space for 3D point cloud semantic segmentation
recovered_records.abstract: In recent years, point cloud semantic segmentation task based on Transformer model has made a major breakthrough. However, the point pairs projected into the Euclidean space are limited by the differences in location information caused by uneven density. In the projection process, there are widespread problems such as unfair local grouping and blurred boundary features. Due to the issues of dislocation or coverage caused by projection to Euclidean space, points with different semantic labels are incorrectly grouped. Therefore, the grouping methods of most Transformer models are unfair, and this phenomenon is particularly obvious in the local boundary region. In order to solve this problem, we propose a Transformer in Hyperbolic space and name it TIH. TIH first maps the points to the special hyperbolic model of the Poincaré disk, and calculates the relative positional relationship of the points using hyperbolic metrics. At the same time, the multi-level feature refusion module is proposed and applied to the Hyperbolic space, which is used to fuse the shallow features that provide boundary information and the deep features that provide semantic information to improve the segmentation effect in the boundary region. The mIoU value of TIH reaches 73.3%, 77.0% and 71.4% respectively by verifying the results on the datasets of S3DIS, ScanNet and SemanticKITTI. Combined with the visual results, it is proven that this paper effectively solves the problems caused by uneven density.

recovered_records.title: A review on artificial intelligence-based medical image enhancement and generation
recovered_records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly important role in medical image generation, contributing to improved image quality and data diversity. These advances are helping to solve key problems in the clinical setting, such as low-quality scans and data sparsity. Initially, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) were mainly utilized, but in recent years, transformer-based models and diffusion models have emerged, leading to technological advances. These latest techniques are being actively researched for their potential for real-world clinical applications. In this paper, AI-based medical image generation techniques are comprehensively investigated, focusing on three major modalities: chest X-ray (CXR), computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). To organize the research, it is divided into two pillars: image enhancement and image synthesis. Image enhancement focuses on directly improving the diagnostic quality of images, including noise removal, blur correction, resolution enhancement, and restoration of incomplete data. Image synthesis, on the other hand, involves techniques that generate new data or improve clinical visibility by augmenting data, restoring anatomical structures, removing occlusions, etc. This paper analyzes the evolution of the model architecture of each approach, as well as the accessibility of the datasets used, code disclosure, quantitative metrics, and clinical evaluation cases involving radiologists. It also diagnoses the current state of medical image generation technologies and discusses future research directions, focusing on key challenges that need to be addressed in the future, such as domain generalization, establishing qualitative evaluation schemes, and integration into clinical workflows.

recovered_records.title: Lightweight quantum recurrent neural networks for time-series and dynamical systems
recovered_records.abstract: We propose two minimal quantum-enhanced recurrent architectures, which are Minimal Quantum Long Short-Term Memory and Minimal Quantum Gated Recurrent Unit that significantly reduce the circuit depth and parameter count of existing Quantum Long Short-Term Memory and Quantum Gated Recurrent Unit models while preserving expressive power. By retaining only the essential variational quantum gates (two per cell) and offloading all remaining operations to lightweight classical layers, our streamlined designs cut runtime by 60% to 75%. We evaluate these four architectures across five ordinary differential equation benchmarks of increasing difficulty: zero-order Bessel-function forecasting, classical Lotka–Volterra predator–prey dynamics, fractional-order Lotka–Volterra, inverse parameter estimation for a damped oscillator, and the stiff Robertson chemical-kinetics system (with a multi-head attention layer). In each experiment, Minimal models match the accuracy of their full-circuit counterparts while training significantly faster. These results demonstrate that judicious pruning of variational circuits yields lightweight quantum-classical hybrids that are both practical for near-term hardware and highly effective on complex time-series and dynamical-system problems.

recovered_records.title: Cross-view graph representation learning model with variational information bottleneck for the association prediction of micro RNA-diseases
recovered_records.abstract: The accurate association mining between micro ribonucleic acids (micro RNA) and diseases could help understand the complex mechanism of diseases. However, the computational algorithms fail to sufficiently extract discriminative patterns from complex biological networks. In this work, we devised a cross-view graph representation learning model based on graph convolution and hierarchical attention with a variational information bottleneck strategy for the potential association prediction of micro RNA-disease pairs. The proposed model not only captures different view-specific similarities, but also discards the noise attribute and superfluous information of nodes. Specifically, our model first built a heterogeneous biological graph by the micro RNA and disease similarity and known associations. Then, the special graph convolutional module is devised to extract the multi-view local interaction features, and the hierarchical attention layer combines the multi-view representation of nodes to capture higher-order discriminative representations. Moreover, the variational information bottleneck retains relevant information while minimizing the redundant features of micro RNA and diseases to obtain discriminative representations. Finally, the adaptive loss function is designed to optimize the performance. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our model in comparison to state-of-the-art models, and indicate that it is a reliable representation learning and prediction model for the micro RNA-disease associations.

recovered_records.title: Physics informed neural network for inertia effect estimation in tunnel boring machine considering time delay
recovered_records.abstract: To quantify the inertia effects in Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs) and mitigate the associated time delay and violent disturbances, this study proposes an inertia estimation method based on the time scale. The theoretical expression of the inertial response time in the Electric-Hydraulic-Mechanical (EHM) systems of a dual-mode TBM is analyzed. A Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) that integrates an encoder-decoder architecture with physical laws is utilized to measure the inertial response time. Based on the estimated inertial response time, a Generative Adversarial Imputation Network (GAIN) detection algorithm is designed to assist operators in diagnosing extreme response scenarios. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through the 1471 samples (training/test:1041/400) from a tunnel excavation experiment, covering various geological conditions such as soft and hard rocks. The results demonstrate that: (1) The proposed PINN model accurately predicts the inertial response time, achieving an R² value of 0.988 under steady-state conditions and 0.980 under unsteady-state conditions. (2) The proposed extreme response detection algorithm reliably diagnoses extreme scenarios, achieving an accuracy of 0.9714, a precision of 0.9042, a recall of 0.9255, and an F1-score of 0.9147. A key contribution of this study is the novel estimation approach for inertia effects in EHM systems, which provides theoretical support for the precise and safe control of TBMs.

recovered_records.title: Contextual information-focused deep learning network for urban road extraction from remote sensing data
recovered_records.abstract: Significant advancements have been made in the extraction of high-resolution remote sensing imagery for urban road detection using deep learning. However, the accuracy of this extraction is still subject to various limitations. First, substantial differences between roads lead to the loss of target contextual information due to standard convolution. Second, the lack of distinct differences between roads and their surrounding environments affects the network's judgment of road boundaries. Third, occluded parts of roads, such as those obscured by trees, are challenging to extract. The present study proposes a deep learning network based on the U-shaped Network (UNet) architecture. Specifically, a multi-scale aggregation module is employed to preserve target contextual information, and a self-attention segmentation module is integrated to reinforce boundary delineation and prevent overfitting between targets and contextual information. A graph convolutional module is ultimately employed for the purpose of global association integration. Specifically, the multi-scale aggregation module effectively integrates information from convolutional kernels of various scales and images of different scales. The graph convolutional module employs the Patch Merging approach to reduce the size of feature maps, thereby obtaining global association information. This approach significantly reduces computational load while ensuring accuracy. The self-attention segmentation module, based on the Sobel operator, strengthens the delineation between targets and their surrounding environments. The proposed modules collectively enhance the Intersection over Union (IoU), F1 score, and Precision by 6.9 %, 5.81 %, and 10.8 %, respectively, in the Massachusetts Roads Dataset. The model as a whole achieves a Mean IoU (MIoU) and F1 score of 76.161 %,73.08 %,76.760 %,76.88 % and 77.262 %,76.00 % in urban road datasets such as Massachusetts Roads Dataset, DeepGlobe Roads Dataset, and Self-Constructed Roads Dataset; in the complex mountainous roads of the Mountain Roads Dataset, the model achieves an MIoU and F1 score of 60.980 % and 41.73 %, respectively.

recovered_records.title: A hybrid deep transfer learning approach for road extraction from high-resolution satellite images based on D-LinkNet and fuzzy systems

This paper proposes an enhanced version of the D-LinkNet model through a hybrid dual-encoder architecture that integrates complementary pre-trained networks, AlexNet or ShuffleNetv2, combined with ResNet34 to capture both fine-grained textures and high-level semantic features. To improve training dynamics and convergence stability, a fuzzy logic-based adaptive learning rate controller is introduced, dynamically adjusting the learning rate based on performance feedback. Additionally, a dynamic loss function combining Binary Cross-Entropy and Dice Loss with adaptive weighting is employed to mitigate class imbalance and preserve road structure continuity. The proposed method is evaluated on two benchmark datasets: DeepGlobe and Massachusetts. Experimental results show that the hybrid-fuzzy model outperforms the baseline D-LinkNet, achieving up to 4.0 % improvement in Intersection over Union (IoU), 6.0 % in F1-score, and 1.94 % in Pixel Accuracy on the Massachusetts dataset, highlighting the practical effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework.

recovered_records.title: MHADFormer: A cost-efficient multiscale hybrid transformer mixer model for automating Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis from MRI scans
recovered_records.abstract: Accurate and early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a critical challenge in clinical neuroscience. Deep learning and vision transformers have advanced automated classification, yet their high computational burden limits deployment in practice. Here, a hybrid architecture, Mixer Hybrid AD Transformer (MHADFormer), is introduced to reconcile accuracy with efficiency through four lightweight modules: the Cost-efficient Feature Extractor (CeFE), Enhanced Mobile Vision Transformer (EMViT), Fused Attention with Cost-efficient Separable Convolutions (FACeS), and Feature Aggregated Spectral Transformer (FAST), integrated with a tailored MLP-Mixer. MHADFormer achieved 99.69 % accuracy on the OASIS dataset and 99.96 % on ADNI, averaging 99.83 %, while requiring only 1.11 M parameters and 0.27 GFLOPs. In addition, the model achieved 81.28 % accuracy in distinguishing between progressive and stable mild cognitive impairment, surpassing state-of-the-art baselines. These results establish MHADFormer as a scalable, interpretable, and resource-aware solution, bridging the gap between deep learning performance and clinical applicability for MRI-based AD diagnosis.

recovered_records.title: Symbolic solution of fractional Volterra population models via physics-informed neural networks and distributed particle swarm optimization
recovered_records.abstract: We propose a distributed hybrid framework for discovering closed-form approximate symbolic (analytical) solutions to fractional Volterra population models, combining grammar-guided Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). The PSO explores a structured symbolic space to construct candidate expressions, while a PINN architecture is used to optimize the internal coefficients of each candidate by minimizing the residual of the governing fractional equation. By distributing fitness evaluation across MPI processes, the swarm achieves greater structural diversity and improved convergence reliability. Extensive experiments across a range of fractional orders (α∈{0.1,0.5,0.9,1.0}) reveal that physically meaningful and accurate symbolic solutions were obtained exclusively via distributed (multi-process) optimization. In all cases, serial (single-process) runs failed to yield any convergent or interpretable expressions, underscoring the necessity of parallel diversity for successful symbolic discovery in these challenging regimes. The discovered expressions are not only accurate but also structurally expressive and interpretable. These results demonstrate that distributed symbolic regression, coupled with physics-informed learning, provides a robust and generalizable approach to symbolic discovery in fractional dynamical systems.

recovered_records.title: Groundwater multi-pollution source tracing method based on encoder decoder residual convolutional neural networks
recovered_records.abstract: Groundwater pollution has become a major threat to the global environment and public health, making the rapid and accurate identification and tracing of pollution sources through scientific methods an urgent necessity. This is critical for formulating effective water management strategies and safeguarding water security, thereby establishing groundwater pollution source identification (GPSI) as an important research field. In this study, we reframe the GPSI challenge as an image-to-image regression task, which can more intuitively capture and map the complex relationships between post-event pollutant concentration distributions and their original sources, thereby improving the accuracy and efficiency of source tracking. We propose an encoder-decoder residual convolutional neural network (EDRCNN) model that integrates residual units and encoder-decoder structures to infer both the location and concentration of pollutants. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed EDRCNN model outperforms other methods, such as artificial neural networks (ANN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and encoder-decoder convolutional neural networks (EDCNN). Specifically, across different scenarios, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) achieved by EDRCNN is significantly lower than that of the best-performing ANN model in comparative tests. Furthermore, EDRCNN predictions yield a lower mean absolute error (MAE) compared to general ANN predictions, and also exhibit superior performance in terms of root mean square error (RMSE), underscoring the superiority of our proposed model in addressing GPSI challenges.

recovered_records.title: A hybrid transformer network with residual-like connections for medical image segmentation
recovered_records.abstract: Medical image segmentation requires models to capture both long-range dependencies and fine spatial details. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) often struggle with global context modeling, while Transformer-based models can incur high computational costs and may miss low-level features. To address these issues, we propose MAT-Unet, a novel U-shaped architecture that introduces two key components: 1) a Mix-Attention Transformer (MAT) module that jointly models local and global dependencies through a Local-Global Self-Attention mechanism and Multi-Head Self-Attention, enhancing contextual understanding while maintaining efficiency; 2) a Residual-like connections (ResPath) to strengthen semantic continuity and long-range information flow between encoder and decoder stages. Experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that MAT-Unet outperforms state-of-the-art CNN and Transformer models in segmentation accuracy. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/CCUTBo/MAT-Unet.

recovered_records.title: Deep learning-enabled fault diagnosis with vision transformers and domain-informed data augmentation for advanced quality control in semiconductor manufacturing
recovered_records.abstract: As fabrication technologies continue to evolve toward finer nodes, the complexity of semiconductor manufacturing processes increases significantly, along with a heightened susceptibility to in-line defects and equipment failures. Addressing these challenges requires a systematic framework that integrates diagnostic intelligence with manufacturing domain knowledge to enhance fault identification and quality control. Despite recent developments in fault detection methodologies, practical limitations persist due to the insufficient integration of domain-specific characteristics and the limited availability of fault data in real-world scenarios. To bridge these gaps, this study proposes an intelligent fault diagnosis approach following the UNISON decision framework, leveraging vision transformer (ViT) for advanced quality control in semiconductor manufacturing. To mitigate the risks of model overfitting caused by imbalanced and sparse data, generative adversarial network (GAN) is employed to augment fault data by embedding domain-relevant process features. Additionally, a heterogeneous data transformation mechanism is proposed to convert one-dimensional data into two-dimensional image representations, thereby enriching feature diversity and enabling effective visual learning. These synthesized image data are then input into a ViT-based deep learning model for process output classification. An empirical study has been conducted on industrial semiconductor manufacturing datasets for validation. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves 99 % classification accuracy, highlighting its practical viability for intelligent fault identification and advanced quality control in semiconductor manufacturing.

recovered_records.title: GCDTA: Graph-attention-assisted contrastive learning for drug-target affinity prediction
recovered_records.abstract: Accurately quantifying Drug–Target Affinity (DTA) remains a fundamental yet unresolved problem in computational pharmacology. Most existing approaches process drug and protein sequences independently and subsequently concatenate their embeddings in a rudimentary fashion, thereby neglecting both the atom-level topology of molecules and richer cross-modality feature interactions. To address these limitations, we propose a novel method called Graph-Attention-Assisted Contrastive Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction (GCDTA). The key idea behind GCDTA is the integration of graph-based structural representations and contrastive learning, enhancing the expressiveness and discriminative capability of learned features. Specifically, GCDTA jointly leverages both structural and sequential information. Molecular graphs of drugs are encoded using Graph Attention Networks (GAT), effectively capturing atom-level topology and local chemical environments. Protein sequences are processed using dilated convolutional layers to capture long-range dependencies and extract essential sequential features. An interactive fusion module is then employed to systematically integrate information from both modalities, enabling more effective and fine-grained cross-modal interactions. Additionally, a tailored contrastive learning objective aligns structurally analogous drug-target pairs, enhancing the discriminative power and robustness of the unified embeddings. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmark datasets demonstrate that GCDTA consistently surpasses current state-of-the-art models, establishing new performance baselines for DTA prediction.

recovered_records.title: Application of physics informed neural networks to partial integro-differential equations in financial modeling and decision making
recovered_records.abstract: In this article, we propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) for solving the single-asset Black-Scholes jump-diffusion models, specifically the Merton and Kou models. PINNs are a scientific machine learning method designed to tackle partial differential equation (PDE) related problems. The partial integro-differential equation is converted into a PDE using integral discretization in order to apply the PINN technique. The training data points are randomly selected from the domain, and the transformed PDE, as well as the initial and boundary conditions, are utilized to construct the loss function. We utilize the hyperbolic tangent function (tanh) as the activation function for the neurons in the hidden layer. The network’s connection weights are optimized using the L-BFGS algorithm. The proposed PINN technique effectively computes the option price and calculates several of its essential Greeks, including Gamma, Theta, and Delta, with no additional overhead. Lastly, we will conduct numerical tests to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach. We will compare it with the conventional numerical method and demonstrate that our technique serves as an effective alternative to competing pricing methods for the Black-Scholes jump-diffusion model.

recovered_records.title: DEJRNN: A novel fusion recurrent neural network-based complex dynamical system modeling and the convergence analysis
recovered_records.abstract: Modeling nonlinear dynamical systems is challenging due to their highly complex, time-varying, and nonlinear behaviors, which conventional modeling approaches often fail to represent accurately. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) offer a data-driven alternative, yet selecting suitable architectures, capturing temporal dependencies, and ensuring convergence stability remain key challenges. This study introduces a novel Diagonal Elman Jordan Recurrent Neural Network (DEJRNN) that synergistically integrates Elman-type hidden feedback, Jordan-type output feedback, and diagonal recurrences within a unified recurrent framework. The model is trained using gradient-descent-based back-propagation, and a Lyapunov-theory-derived adaptive learning rate ensures convergence, stability, and robustness. Performance evaluation across four complex nonlinear dynamical systems reveals that, during training, DEJRNN achieves up to 72% and 47% reductions in average mean-squared and mean-absolute errors, respectively, compared to standard RNNs (ERNN, JRNN, DRNN). In testing, these reductions reach 41% and 29%, confirming excellent generalization capability under unseen, noisy, and time-varying inputs. The Lyapunov-based adaptive learning mechanism not only guarantees stable convergence but also alleviates gradient vanishing and enhances dynamic tracking accuracy. Overall, the DEJRNN framework provides a compact, interpretable, and computationally efficient solution for nonlinear system modeling, combining the structural simplicity of traditional RNNs with analytical convergence assurance. The proposed model establishes a strong foundation for developing future stability-driven neural architectures for real-time modeling and control applications.

recovered_records.title: Dynamic scene understanding of surgical medical images for accurate disease diagnosis using deep learning based motion segmentation

Understanding the nature of dynamic factors in the surgical environment is a significant challenge. Understanding and analyzing movements in the field of surgery is important because they are constantly changing due to surgeon actions and biological tissue responses. A robust visual perspective is critical for interpreting changes in the field of surgery over time, with a strong emphasis on understanding movement mechanisms that promote surgical progression and tissue survival. To address this challenge, a deep learning-based model for segmentation in dynamic scenes is presented. It allows more accurate and predictable identification of moving organs rather than intra-operatively damaged tissue. The research begins with the development of an optimal method for organ dynamics analysis in cross-sectional image processing using the enhanced orca predation optimization (EOPO) algorithm. A hybrid model is proposed that combines different trained models with stochastic differential equation (SDE) to deal with the nonlinear behavior inherent in SDEs. It helps to identify unusual changes and changing motion patterns, providing more accurate traffic distribution. In addition, a prediction model using deep graph neural network (DGNN) is used to predict future movements of organs, which contributes to the direction of improvement identified using CholecSeg8K data. The proposed DGNN models show the mean accuracy of 99.125 % and mean IoU of 98.808 % which is 1.538 % and 1.121 % efficient than the existing models. recovered_records.title: On the value of uncertainty quantification in deep learning based breast cancer molecular subtype classification
recovered_records.abstract: Cancer is still a major global health issue and one of the leading causes of death globally. Despite significant progress in the field of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) in the medical field and especially in cancer research, uncertainty quantification has been largely under-investigated, resulting in the development of decision systems with questionable reliability and confidence, which are essential for effective integration and adoption in a clinical context. In this study, we evaluate and discuss five uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods: Single Deterministic, Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD), Bayesian Neural Network based on Variational Inference (BNN), Deep Ensemble (DE), and Bootstrap Ensemble (BG) for the identification of breast cancer molecular subtype using a deep neural network (DNN). These empirical evaluations were based, in addition to the classical classification performance criteria such as accuracy, recall, precision and f1 score, on other advanced criteria related to sensibility, interpretability, robustness, and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. Moreover, we introduce and evaluate new algorithms for synthetic OOD data generation, crucial for assessing the reliability of quantified uncertainties. Results indicated that Ensemble-based UQ methods generally provided more robust uncertainty estimates and performed best in terms of sensitivity. Stochastic methods, on the other hand, achieved superior calibration, with Bayesian Neural Networks in particular demonstrating strong robustness to adversarial attacks, an attribute that may enhance the generalization capacity of classifiers. Overall, we found that uncertainty estimates not only provide reliable confidence measures but also enhance the transparency of model predictions, supporting safer clinical deployment.

recovered_records.title: Memory bank-guided diffusion model for lightweight anomaly detection
recovered_records.abstract: Reconstruction-based image anomaly detection models that utilize diffusion models have shown superior performance in recent studies. However, these models suffer from substantial computational overhead and inference latency, limiting their deployment in practical applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce LAMBDA, a lightweight diffusion-based framework that leverages memory bank-guided denoising for efficient anomaly detection. Our approach introduces two key components: (1) Memory Bank-guided denoising that leverages pre-stored normal latent representations to achieve both computational efficiency and superior reconstruction fidelity, leading to more accurate anomaly localization and (2) Guidance Scale Map, which dynamically adjusts guidance intensity based on dataset distributions. Experimental results show that LAMBDA achieves an 80.8 % reduction in GPU memory consumption during training and 53.2 % during inference, while achieving 2.3× and 3.5× speedup in training and inference times, respectively, compared to the baseline. Despite these efficiency gains, LAMBDA maintains competitive performance, achieving accuracy on par with state-of-the-art models. These results demonstrate the potential of our approach for real-world industrial applications, offering a resource-efficient solution for diffusion-based image anomaly detection.

recovered_records.title: Reinforcement learning-driven adaptive intelligence for phytochemical optimization in cannabis cultivation using precision agriculture
recovered_records.abstract: Optimizing cannabis cultivation to enhance phytochemical production requires navigating complex, non-linear interactions among environmental factors including soil composition, nutrient management, planting density, and harvest timing. Traditional single-factor optimization approaches fail to address multi-objective trade-offs inherent in maximizing competing phytochemicals—tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), cannabidiol (CBD), tetrahydrocannabivarin (THCV), cannabinol (CBN), and terpenes—simultaneously. This study develops and validates an integrated framework combining D-optimal (determinant-optimal) experimental design, regression modeling, and Reinforcement Learning-driven Adaptive Multiple Intelligence System (RL-AMIS) for multi-objective cannabis cultivation optimization. Using "Hang Kra Rog Phu Phan," a Thai landrace cultivar, we conducted 73 strategically designed treatments under controlled greenhouse conditions to develop predictive models quantifying cultivation-phytochemistry relationships. RL-AMIS, benchmarked against standard metaheuristics (Artificial Bee Colony, Whale Optimization Algorithm, Differential Evolution, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and original Adaptive Multiple Intelligence System), achieved superior computational performance with Hypervolume of 0.67 and Average Pareto Points of 1.6, compared to 0.36–0.40 for conventional approaches. Critically, field validation of one optimal parameter set across five replicate trials demonstrated that computationally optimized parameters achieved predicted phytochemical profiles with less than 0.3 % deviation, providing proof-of-concept that the framework bridges the theory-practice gap prevalent in agricultural optimization research. We position this as applied research emphasizing systematic integration and empirical validation rather than algorithmic novelty. While regression coefficients are cultivar-specific to "Hang Kra Rog Phu Phan," the optimization framework methodology is applicable to other cultivars requiring similar multi-objective phytochemical optimization, though each requires cultivar-specific parameterization. This work provides a validated, resource-efficient methodology (73 vs. 8748 full factorial runs) for evidence-based cultivation decisions and demonstrates the value of integrating computational optimization with precision agriculture for medical cannabis production under controlled conditions.

recovered_records.title: Gradual machine learning for medical image classification via evolutionary feature fusion
recovered_records.abstract: Medical image classification (MIC) is a critical task in the medical imaging field. Recently, deep learning (DL) techniques, represented by convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in MIC. However, in many medical fields, the scarcity of labeled data makes DL models highly sensitive to data distribution. Moreover, most MIC methods rely on a single DL backbone, resulting in limited robustness. To address these issues, we propose a learning paradigm that does not assume independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data, gradual machine learning (GML), via evolutionary feature fusion for MIC. It leverages the optimized feature vectors to construct factors for test images and iteratively labels them through factor graph inference. Specifically, we first use multiple DL backbones to extract multi-view complementary feature vectors from medical images and effectively concatenate them. We then propose a novel multi-population evolutionary algorithm (MPEA) to perform feature selection (FS) on the concatenated feature vectors, effectively removing redundant features to achieve deep fusion. Finally, GML extracts evidence factors for test images from the optimized feature vectors to facilitate gradual inference. The proposed MPEA optimizes the population initialization strategy, environmental selection strategy and evolutionary operators to enhance the efficacy of the resulting features as a mechanism for gradual inference. Extensive experiments conducted on eight medical datasets demonstrate that our method achieves higher and more stable classification performance compared to the existing SOTA methods.

recovered_records.title: PFADet: A few-shot prompt-guided fabric anomaly detection network using Large Vision-Language Models
recovered_records.abstract: Fabric anomaly detection (FAD) is crucial in guaranteeing fabric quality and optimizing production processes. Despite the progress of fully supervised methods in FAD tasks, the scarcity of anomaly samples and the difficulty of high-quality pixel-level labeling have motivated the attention on few-shot learning. Meanwhile, Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) excel with strong cross-modal understanding, whereas detection accuracy and adaptability are limited in FAD due to insufficient prior knowledge and missing multimodal data. To this end, we propose a few-shot prompt-guided fabric anomaly detection network (PFADet), based on LVLMs for efficient detection and fine-grained localization. Specifically, adaptive fabric text description templates construct customized descriptions for different fabric types to achieve cross-modal feature alignment, effectively capturing the subtle differences between local and global anomaly features. Integrated Prompt Module leverages the Weight Dynamic Distribution Network (DDNet) to achieve multi-scale feature fusion, providing interpretive feedback and interactive queries that support the anomaly detection results. Additionally, combined with the improved loss function, the discrimination between normal and abnormal features is enhanced by dynamically adjusting the sample boundary weights. Extensive experiments on fabric datasets and generalization analysis on publicly available industrial benchmark datasets demonstrate that PFADet outperforms existing methods in both image-level localization and pixel-level segmentation under few-shot settings, achieving image-AUC of 98.6 %/93.0 %, pixel-AUC of 91.4 %/87.2 %, accuracy of 90.4 %/92.0 %, and F1-score of 0.4441/0.5656 on Color-F and Rollei datasets under 1-shot setting.

recovered_records.title: Physics-informed neural control for mitigating flood effects: A case study based on a simulated hydrographic basin
recovered_records.abstract: This study presents a novel flood mitigation strategy in hydrographic basins that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with Model Predictive Control (MPC). The PINN-based MPC computes optimal dam floodgate (opening and closing) signals to minimize water level excess at critical downstream points while ensuring reservoir management during flood events. The methodology uses PINNs as surrogate models for the Saint-Venant equations in the modeling process, producing accurate hydrodynamic descriptions of river channels with reduced computational demand for optimal control. The PINN model predicts water levels and flows across space and time, assisting control decisions without the high costs typically associated with solving complex partial differential equations. The proposed control framework is evaluated in a simulated hydrographic basin composed of two reservoirs and four interconnected channels with lengths ranging from 10 to 68 km, bed slopes of 0.0025, and Manning coefficients of 0.02. The channels feature variable cross-sections, varying from 45 to 95 m widths. In the modeling process, PINNs accurately approximate the hydrodynamic behavior in each channel, achieving MAPE between 0.63 % and 2.74 % for water levels and 0.03 %–0.42 % for flow rates, even under initial and boundary conditions not present in the training dataset. In extreme inflow scenarios for the case study, the PINN-based MPC framework effectively managed flood conditions by dynamically adjusting control signals, preventing flooding in downstream urban areas. The experiments revealed that the PINN-MPC approach provides a scalable, computationally efficient alternative for real-time flood control, with the potential for broader applications in hydrological management.

recovered_records.title: A two-stage symbolic regression method for discovering mathematical formulas
recovered_records.abstract: In this study, we propose a two-stage symbolic regression method with hybrid optimization for discovering mathematical formulas. Unlike existing approaches such as genetic programming, which attempt to optimize both model structure and parameters simultaneously, the proposed method decouples the process into two distinct stages. In the first stage, a genetic algorithm is employed to generate a diverse and high-quality pool of candidate terms from the given variables and operators. In the second stage, simulated annealing (SA) and a reinforcement learning-enhanced SA (RLSA) method are jointly utilized to solve a subset selection problem—aiming to identify the optimal subset of terms that best fit an equation via linear regression. The effectiveness of the proposed method was evaluated on five benchmark datasets comprising 56 widely used instances. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms five state-of-the-art baselines in accurately recovering ground-truth formulas. Furthermore, in a case study on triangle area formula discovery, the proposed method successfully identified 295 valid formulas, surpassing the 251 known formulas reported in the literature. These findings suggest that the proposed hybrid optimization design, leveraging the complementary strengths of different metaheuristics, is well-suited for navigating complex search spaces and achieving competitive performance in symbolic regression tasks.

recovered_records.title: Improving hydrologic prediction and interpretability through physics-informed dual-output LSTM with water and energy balance constraints
recovered_records.abstract: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has demonstrated strong predictive skill in hydrological modelling, but often lacks physical consistency and interpretability. The Mass-conserving LSTM (MC-LSTM) overcomes this limitation by enforcing water balance, yet the existing formulations remain restricted to single-variable prediction and simplified representation of hydrological fluxes. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Dual-Output LSTM (PIDuaL) that simultaneously predicts streamflow and evapotranspiration (ET) through a modified mass-balance structure. Three constrained variants are further developed by enforcing water balance, energy balance, and combined water and energy balance within the PIDuaL framework. For fair benchmark comparison, a purely data-driven Dual-LSTM is also implemented. Across 149 human-influenced watersheds in India, LSTM and Dual-LSTM show lower streamflow skill, with a median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.58, whereas MC-LSTM and PIDuaL improve performance to a median NSE of 0.67. Performance gains are most pronounced in hydrologically challenging conditions, including semi-arid and highly human-influenced watersheds, where purely data-driven models struggle. PIDuaL substantially reduces bias, and its constrained variants exhibit the largest improvement in low-flow simulation, accompanied by stronger correlation with baseflow-governing attributes, indicating physically meaningful recession dynamics. recovered_records.title: Quantifying multidimensional drought risks under climate change: A deep learning-based downscaling and DDF curves approach
recovered_records.abstract: Reliable estimates of future drought characteristics and associated risks are essential for regional water resource planning under climate change. Traditional large-scale precipitation datasets and the derived drought indices, such as the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), suffer from limitations in spatial resolution and cannot directly represent actual precipitation deficits or associated water shortages. Moreover, separate analyses of drought duration, severity, and frequency often fail to capture the interdependence among these characteristics. To address these limitations, this study develops an integrated analytical framework that combines multi-criteria GCM selection, deep learning-based ensemble downscaling, and drought Duration-Deficit-Frequency (DDF) analysis. Future precipitation projections at the analyzed stations in the Upper Yangtze River Basin are first generated under four SSP scenarios through the proposed downscaling framework. The downscaled series are then used to construct DDF curves based on the best-fit probability distribution, jointly quantifying drought durations, cumulative precipitation deficits, and return periods. The results indicate that the occurrence of extreme droughts generally exceeds historical levels under future climate scenarios, although the magnitude of change varies substantially among the analyzed stations and across SSP scenarios. DDF analysis further reveals increased cumulative precipitation deficits, particularly for longer-duration drought events. Bootstrap analysis indicates that uncertainty in the DDF curves increases with drought duration and return period, while multilevel factorial analysis (MFA) identifies GCM ensemble configuration and downscaling methodology as the dominant sources of uncertainty. By linking drought-index-based event identification with physical precipitation-deficit quantification, the proposed framework provides a physically interpretable and uncertainty-aware approach for assessing station-specific drought characteristics and associated risks under alternative SSP scenarios.
